function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common “tools” (websites, apps, APIs, and platforms) you can use to book flights:

| Category | Tool / Service | What it offers | Typical use‑case |
|----------|----------------|----------------|------------------|
| **Online travel agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Aggregates flights, hotels, car rentals, packages. | One‑stop booking for multi‑service trips. |
| | **Kayak** | Flight comparison engine, price alerts, flexible date search. | Finding the cheapest fare across many carriers. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Global flight search, price alerts, “whole month” view. | Great for budget travelers and flexible dates. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast search, price graph, “Explore” map. | Quick fare comparison and itinerary planning. |
| | **Momondo** | Price comparison, “price calendar”, “price alerts”. | Good for spotting hidden deals. |
| | **Priceline** | “Name Your Own Price” and “Express Deals” for last‑minute savings. | Bargain hunting for flights & hotels. |
| | **Orbitz** | Similar to Expedia, often bundled with hotel points. | Frequent flyer points integration. |
| | **Travelocity** | OTA with “Price Match Guarantee”. | General travel booking. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” deals for flights & hotels. | Last‑minute discounted fares. |
| | **CheapOair** | Discounted fares, promo codes. | Budget travelers looking for coupons. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels but also offers flights. | One‑stop booking for accommodation + flight. |
| | **Trip.com** | Global OTA, strong presence in Asia. | International travelers, especially in Asia. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Price alerts, coupon codes. | Tracking specific routes for deals. |
| | **Hipmunk** | “Best Time to Fly” feature, “Travel Score”. | Planning trips with best value. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Curated travel deals, coupons. | Finding curated flight deals. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Last‑minute flight & package deals. | Impulse bookings. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA, flight + hotel bundles. | European travelers. |
| | **eDreams** | Cheap flights, “Price Drop” alerts. | Budget travelers. |
| | **TUI** | Travel agency with flights, hotels, cruises. | All‑in‑one travel packages. |
| | **Travelgenio** | OTA with flight + hotel combos. | General travel booking. |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network, flight search API. | Developers building flight search widgets. |

### 2. Airline‑direct booking tools

| Tool | What it offers | Why you’d use it |
|------|----------------|------------------|
| **Direct airline websites** (e.g., Delta.com, United.com, Air France, Emirates) | Full fare classes, loyalty miles, seat selection, baggage options. | Best for frequent flyers who want to use miles or want the most accurate fare info. |
| **Airline mobile apps** | Push notifications for price drops, mobile‑only discounts, boarding passes. | Handy for last‑minute changes and mobile‑friendly itineraries. |
| **Airline APIs** (e.g., Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport, Skyscanner API) | Programmatic flight search, booking, and fare rules. | Used by developers building custom booking engines or integrating flight data into other services. |
| **Frequent‑flyer portals** (e.g., United MileagePlus, Delta SkyMiles) | Earn and redeem miles, elite status benefits. | Ideal for loyal customers who want to maximize mileage accrual and redemption. |

---

### 3. Meta‑search engines & price‑comparison tools

| Tool | Key features | When to use |
|------|--------------|-------------|
| **Google Flights** | Instant price graph, “Explore” map, price alerts. | Quick fare comparison and itinerary planning. |
| **Skyscanner** | “Whole month” view, price alerts, “Everywhere” search. | Great for flexible travelers looking for the cheapest month. |
| **Kayak** | Price alerts, “Price forecast” predictions, bundle options. | Useful for tracking future price trends. |
| **Momondo** | “Price calendar,” “Price alerts,” “Price comparison.” | Good for spotting hidden deals. |
| **Hopper** | Predictive pricing, “Book now” vs. “Wait” suggestions. | Helpful for long‑term planning. |
| **Airfarewatchdog** | Coupon codes, price alerts. | Good for coupon‑savvy travelers. |
| **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network, flight search API. | For developers building flight widgets or earning commissions. |

---

### 4. Mobile‑first & niche booking apps

| App | Focus | Why it matters |
|-----|-------|----------------|
| **Hopper** | Predictive pricing, mobile UI | Great for “wait‑or‑book” decisions. |
| **Kiwi.com** | “Virtual interlining” (mixing airlines), low‑cost fares | Enables cheaper itineraries that traditional OTAs miss. |
| **Ryanair** | Low‑cost European flights | Direct booking for budget travelers. |
| **EasyJet** | Low‑cost European flights | Direct booking for budget travelers. |
| **Southwest** | U.S. domestic flights, no change fees | Direct booking for U.S. travelers. |
| **Airbnb Experiences** | Flights + experiences | For travelers wanting integrated travel + activities. |
| **TripIt** | Trip organizer, flight alerts | Helps keep itineraries organized. |

---

### 5. Developer‑centric flight‑booking APIs

| API | Provider | Highlights |
|-----|----------|------------|
| **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Amadeus | Flight search, booking, fare rules, seat availability. |
| **Sabre APIs** | Sabre | Comprehensive travel data, booking, loyalty integration. |
| **Travelport APIs** | Travelport | Global distribution system (GDS) data, booking. |
| **Skyscanner API** | Skyscanner | Search, price alerts, flight data. |
| **FlightAware API** | FlightAware | Real‑time flight status, historical data. |
| **OpenSky API** | OpenSky | Real‑time flight tracking. |
| **Google Flights API** (unofficial) | Google | Not officially public, but some third‑party wrappers exist. |
| **FlightStats API** | FlightStats | Flight status, delay predictions. |

These APIs let you build custom booking widgets, integrate flight data into your own app, or automate price monitoring.

---

### 6. Things to keep in mind

| Topic | Tips |
|-------|------|
| **Fare rules & taxes** | OTAs sometimes hide taxes or fees; check the airline’s site for the exact breakdown. |
| **Seat selection & baggage** | Many airlines charge extra for seats and checked bags; OTAs may bundle them at a discount or not show them at all. |
| **Loyalty miles** | Booking directly with the airline usually gives you the most miles and status credit. |
| **Price alerts** | Use multiple alert services (Google Flights, Skyscanner, Hopper) to catch the best deal. |
| **Hidden fees** | Low‑cost carriers (Ryanair, EasyJet, Southwest) often have hidden fees for extras; read the fine print. |
| **Mobile‑only discounts** | Some airlines offer exclusive mobile‑app discounts; download the app if you’re booking on the go. |
| **API rate limits** | When using flight APIs, watch out for rate limits and caching strategies. |
| **Data accuracy** | Flight data can change quickly; always double‑check the airline’s official website before finalizing. |

---

### Bottom line

- **For casual travelers**: Use OTAs like Expedia, Kayak, Skyscanner, or Google Flights for quick comparisons and price alerts.  
- **For budget travelers**: Check low‑cost carriers directly (Ryanair, EasyJet, Southwest) and use meta‑search engines that highlight cheap fares.  
- **For frequent flyers**: Book directly with the airline to maximize miles and status benefits.  
- **For developers**: Leverage APIs from Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport, or Skyscanner to build custom booking solutions.  

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper dives into any specific platform, API, or booking strategy!
